headline: High: Plandex can write and egress by default, while the paired open-source hub has no documented isolation or runtime controls, creating unsafe interaction and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads files and stdin/stdout and can apply plan outputs; the hub is an open-source agent/RAG/MCP-oriented repo with no runtime isolation documented. If the hub’s content is copied into Plandex or shared via files, instruction-like text could be treated as trusted. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the hub’s generated text is pasted into Plandex prompts or files
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled on content originating from the hub
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Keep hub outputs in a separate folder from Plandex workspaces
Add a manual review step before any apply
Prefix imported text with provenance labels
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware prompt filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while the hub shows no data classes touched and no filesystem or network surface documented. A leakage path exists only if sensitive files are placed into Plandex’s project directory; the hub itself does not document sensitive-data handling. The pairwise risk is therefore limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Plandex’s project directory
IF Plandex is configured to send those files to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared project directory
Use a redacted sample workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys
Restrict outbound domains at the network layer
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the hub is an open-source agent repo with no runtime write controls documented. If both are used on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git-state conflicts are plausible. Uncertainty about the hub’s runtime behavior escalates this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree
IF Plandex and the hub both modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or serialized commits
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex’s review-then-apply flow can act on upstream text, and the hub is tagged for agents/LLMs/RAG, so its outputs could become inputs to Plandex without verification. That creates a plausible chain where one agent’s generated content is treated as authoritative by the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF the hub’s outputs are fed into Plandex as task instructions or code
IF Plandex applies changes without an independent verification step
mitigations: Require human review of upstream outputs
Add a checksum or citation check before apply
Separate generation and execution roles
Log source provenance for every imported artifact
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Plandex explicitly handles model-provider API keys and sends data to cloud or self-hosted servers, while the hub has no residency or retention policy documented. This is a compliance gap rather than a proven breach; the other agent is not cited because no specific residency claim is documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is entered into Plandex
IF the deployment uses a third-party model provider without a DPA or retention review
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Plandex
Review provider retention settings
Use a self-hosted model endpoint
Document data handling for the workspace
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
